healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system with limited capacity. Tupua Tamasese Meaole Hospital (TTM) in Apia is the main facility. District hospitals on Upolu and Savai'i provide basic care. Private clinics available in Apia.
qualityNotes: Basic healthcare available in Apia. TTM Hospital handles most conditions but equipment and specialist availability are limited. Rural areas and villages have very basic health posts. Serious conditions require evacuation to New Zealand or Australia. Decompression chamber not available locally.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-4:30pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. Very limited hours and availability outside Apia.
pharmacyTips: Bring all medications you need, especially if visiting Savai'i or rural areas. The hospital pharmacy and a few private pharmacies in Apia carry basic medications. Staff speak English and Samoan.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications require a doctor's prescription. Bring adequate supplies of all prescription medications as availability is very limited. Keep medications in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Samoa has strict drug laws.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine products
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled due to misuse concerns. Bring documentation if carrying.

bringDocumentation: Bring prescriptions, a doctor's letter, travel insurance documentation, and copies of vaccination records. English documentation is fine.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended. Ensure your policy covers medical evacuation to New Zealand, as serious conditions cannot be treated locally. Many activities like snorkeling and hiking should be covered.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue and Zika are present — use insect repellent. Samoa experienced a measles outbreak in 2019; ensure MMR vaccination is up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water quality varies. Use bottled or boiled water as a precaution, especially in rural areas and villages. Apia water supply is generally treated but can be affected by heavy rain.
foodSafetyTips: Food at hotels and established restaurants is generally safe. Be cautious with raw seafood and food from roadside stalls. Tropical fruit is abundant and safe when peeled. Wash hands frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Samoa is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialized care are evacuated to New Zealand (Auckland) or Australia.
sources: New Zealand Ministry of Health Travel Advice
metaDescription: Samoa health guide for travelers: hospitals, pharmacies, vaccinations, water safety, and emergency info.

hospitals.name: Tupua Tamasese Meaole Hospital (TTM)
hospitals.notes: Main national hospital. Handles emergency and general care. English spoken. Limited specialist equipment. 24/7 emergency department.

hospitals.name: Malietoa Tanumafili II Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on Savai'i island. Basic care only. For serious conditions, transfer to Apia or evacuation required.

hospitals.name: Samoa General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Basic dental services at TTM Hospital and a few private dentists in Apia. None on Savai'i or rural areas.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic. Bring dental supplies and address dental issues before traveling.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, go to TTM Hospital dental clinic in Apia or a private dentist in the Apia area.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated crisis hotline available in Samoa.
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy or use international crisis lines such as Crisis Text Line.
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. A few counselors available through hospitals and NGOs in Apia.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Cultural stigma remains significant. Consider telehealth with your home-country provider for ongoing mental health support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Samoa. Few buildings have wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: TTM Hospital has basic wheelchair access. Smaller health facilities may not be accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads can be rough. Taxis are the best option but vehicles may not be wheelchair-friendly.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact accommodations in advance about accessibility. Beach fales (traditional open-air huts) are generally not wheelchair accessible. Plan carefully for mobility needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at TTM Hospital in Apia.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity is very limited. Bring personal health supplies including masks and hand sanitizer.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain receipts and medical documentation from the treating facility. Most care requires upfront payment. Submit insurance claims upon return home with all original documentation.

commonCosts.currency: WST (Samoan Tala), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Public hospital costs are low but facilities are basic. Private clinic costs are higher. Cash payment is standard.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation to New Zealand is the standard route for serious conditions. Regular flights to Auckland make this the fastest option. Ensure travel insurance covers evacuation.
